rationale: Fixture-only overhead as C11 defines it (fixture entry minus production entry): 154,465 B gzip. Most of it is signed-in application code that the production build loads lazily after sign-in (production lazy chunks sum to about 215 kB gzip, so production entry plus lazy is about 324 kB against the fixture's 263 kB entry plus 117 kB lazy); the fixture is a proxy for the signed-in shell, not a measurement of production's signed-in cost.

Loading beside size (P-1S, Chromium, CDP-emulated throttling with 4x CPU on the Air desktop, three cold runs each, medians and ranges): the fixture entry's first contentful paint is 132 ms later than production's on fast 4G (300 [288-332] vs 168 [164-176] ms, mobile viewport) and 228 ms later on slow 4G (796 [772-800] vs 568 [568-572] ms); largest contentful paint is about 2.0 s on slow 4G for both (1,952 [1,944-1,960] fixture vs 2,040 [2,016-2,040] ms production) and about 0.5 s on fast 4G. Read as a linear order of magnitude, about 1.5 ms of slow-4G first contentful paint per kB of initial JavaScript gzip.

Headroom: 10 % of 262,856 is 26,286 B, about 38-39 ms of emulated slow-4G first contentful paint by that reading, within twice the run-to-run FCP range observed (up to 28 ms on slow 4G, 44 ms on fast 4G). No performance cliff was observed or is claimed; no responsiveness target is set.

Expected growth: the four named branches not in this build recorded their growth: WEB-13a about 2.6 kB (243,097 against the 240,479-byte main of 10 October, its decision's comparison), WEB-08d 4,234 B (its author's attribution against its base); WEB-14a and WEB-08c record overruns of 2,021 and 426 B over the old 241,544 ceiling, about 3.1 kB and 1.5 kB above that 240,479-byte main (an approximation: their own bases are not recorded). As an estimate of DELTAS only (branch bundles are not additive and none is a measurement of the combined application), about 11.4 kB of 26.3 kB, leaving about 14.9 kB (about 5.7 %) for chunk-layout effects and unattributed growth before an explicit decision is needed.

Why 10 % rather than less or more: 5 % (13.1 kB) would leave about 1.7 kB after the named branches, so the first integration would need another decision with no evidence of benefit; a larger figure has no measured basis and would weaken the guard as a regression detector. The 10 % tolerance is therefore kept, as OD-2 permits, for reasons stated here rather than by default.
